'''Charles Richard Francis Maunder''' (23 November 1937 – 5 June 2018) was a British mathematician and musicologist.

==Early life==
Maunder was educated at the [[Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe]], and [[Jesus College, Cambridge]], before going on to complete a [[PhD]] at [[Christ’s College, Cambridge]], in 1962. After teaching at [[Southampton University]] he became a fellow of Christ’s in 1964.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2018/jul/11/richard-maunder-obituary |title=Richard Maunder obituary |newspaper=The Guardian |date=11 July 2018}}</ref>

==Mathematics==
Maunder's field of work was [[algebraic topology]]. He used [[Postnikov system]]s to give an alternative construction of the [[Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence]]. With this construction, the differentials can be better described.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Nobuyuki |last1=Oda |first2=Yoshimi |last2=Shitanda |title=On the unstable homotopy spectral sequences |journal=Manuscripta Mathematica |volume=56 |issue=1 |year=1986 |issn=0025-2611 |pages=19–35 |doi=10.1007/BF01171031|s2cid=122846873 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite arXiv |first1=Daniel |last1=Grady |first2=Hisham |last2=Sati |title=Spectral sequences in smooth generalized cohomology |year=2016 |class=math.AT |eprint=1605.03444v1 }}</ref> The family of higher [[cohomology operation]]s on mod-2 cohomology that he constructed has been discussed by several authors.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=J.F. |last1=McLendon |title=Higher order twisted cohomology operations |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=7 |issue=3 |year=1969 |pages=183–214 |doi=10.1007/BF01404305|bibcode=1969InMat...7..183M |s2cid=119895355 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |first1=Samuel |last1=Gitler |first2=James |last2=Milgram |editor-first=Peter J. |editor-last=Hilton |title=Unstable divisibility of the chern character |encyclopedia=Symposium on Algebraic Topology |publisher=Battelle Seattle Research Center |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |year=1971 |volume=249 |isbn=3-540-05715-3 |pages=31–33 |doi=10.1007/BFb0060893}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |first1=José |last1=Adem |first2=Kee Yuen |last2=Lam |chapter=Evaluation of some Maunder cohomology operations |editor1-first=Jacob |editor1-last=Palis |editor2-first=Manfredo |editor2-last=do Carmo |editor2-link=Manfredo do Carmo |title=Geometry and Topology |publisher=III Latin American School of Mathematics |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |year=1977 |volume=597 |isbn=3-540-08345-6 |pages=1–31 |doi=10.1007/BFb0085345}}</ref> In 1981 he gave a short proof of the [[Kan-Thurston theorem]],<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=C.R.F. |last1=Maunder |title=A Short Proof of a Theorem of Kan and Thurston |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |volume=13 |issue=4 |year=1981 |pages=325–327 |doi=10.1112/blms/13.4.325}}</ref> according to which for every [[Connected space#Path connectedness|path-connected]] [[topological space]] X there is a [[discrete group]] π such that there is a [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] [[isomorphism]] of the [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] K(π,1) after X. His textbook ''Algebraic Topology'' (1970) continues to circulate in the 1996 Dover edition.

==Musicology==
Maunder created a new version of [[Requiem (Mozart)|Mozart's Requiem]]. Following on from other musicologists such as [[Ernst Hess (composer)|Ernst Hess]], [[Franz Beyer (musicologist)|Franz Beyer]] and [[Robert Levin (musicologist)|Robert D. Levin]], he presented a fundamental revision of Mozart's last work, in which, like his predecessors, he wanted to remove [[Franz Xaver Süssmayr|Süssmayr]]'s additions as far as possible and replace them with Mozart's own ideas. This new version was recorded by [[Christopher Hogwood]] with the [[Academy of Ancient Music]] in 1983 and the score was published in 1988.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Paul |last1=Moseley |title=Requiem, K. 626 by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Franz Beyer, Richard Maunder |type=Review |journal=Music & Letters |volume=70 |issue=4 |year=1989 |issn=0027-4224 |pages=588–590 |doi=10.1093/ml/70.4.588 |jstor=736022}}</ref> In 1992 it was recorded by {{ill|Rupert Gottfried Frieberger|de}}.<ref>{{Cite news |first1=W.-E. |last1=von Lewinski |title=''Alt klingend, neu gefaßt: Mozarts Requiem unter Frieberger und Norrington'' |newspaper=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |date=1992-11-14}}.</ref>

In doing so, Maunder rejected Süssmayr's ''Sanctus'' and ''Benedictus'' completely and removed them from the work; he considered only the ''Agnus Dei'' to be authentic because of its comparisons with other church music works by Mozart. Maunder also composed an ''Amen'' fugue for the conclusion of the ''Lacrimosa'', for which he took Mozart's sketch sheet and a fugue for organ roll by Mozart ({{ill|K.&nbsp;608|fr|Fantaisie en fa mineur pour orgue mécanique, K. 608}}) as a starting point. He also fundamentally revised Süssmayr's instrumentation throughout the Requiem.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Paul |last1=Moseley |title=''Mozart's Requiem: On Preparing a New Edition'' by Richard Maunder |type=Review |journal=Music & Letters |volume=70 |issue=4 |year=1989 |issn=0027-4224 |pages=545–547 |doi=10.1093/ml/70.4.545 |jstor=735996}}</ref> 

This version was performed several times in German-speaking countries, including a dance version ''Requiem!'' by {{ill|Birgit Scherzer|de}}.

Maunder's edition of Mozart's [[Great Mass in C minor, K. 427|C minor Mass]] was published in 1990<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Denis |last1=McCaldin |title=Mozart, Wolfgang Amadeus, Mass in C Minor K.427, ed. Richard Maunder |type=Full score/vocal score |journal=Music & Letters |volume=72 |issue=2 |year=1991 |issn=0027-4224 |pages=332–334 |doi=10.1093/ml/72.2.332 |jstor=735744}}</ref> and was first recorded by Hogwood in the same year.
Maunder edited also pieces by Francesco Geminiani, Tomaso Albinoni, Henry Purcell, members of the Bach Family, Giuseppe Sammartini and others.
https://imslp.org/wiki/Category:Maunder,_Richard
